name: Variable Impedance Rifle VIR-9 'Switchback'
description:
The VIR-9 is a linear magnetically accelerated rifle that distinguishes itself through its real-time impedance modulation system. Conventional gauss rifles fix their magnetic coil parameters at manufacture, producing a consistent velocity and terminal profile. The Switchback instead allows the operator to adjust coil impedance across a 12-stage spectrum between shots, changing the projectile's exit velocity, spin rate, and electromagnetic emission profile on the fly. A low-impedance shot exits at subsonic velocity with minimal EM signature, functioning as a near-silent precision round. Maximum impedance produces a hypervelocity dart capable of defeating most structural barriers short of military-grade composite plating.

Tessera Corponation developed the VIR-9 for private security forces that operate across highly variable threat environments where carrying multiple weapon systems is impractical. The 12-stage impedance selector is mounted as a rotating collar around the trigger guard, operable with the firing hand without breaking grip — a deliberate ergonomic priority that took four design iterations to achieve. The rifle feeds from a 15-round magazine of ferromagnetic tungsten darts, each identical; the variation in terminal effect is produced entirely by the electromagnetic system rather than by different projectile types.

The weapon's primary limitation is thermal management. Running sustained fire at high-impedance settings causes the coil array to overheat, and the VIR-9 includes an automatic throttle that forces a 4-second cooling interval after three consecutive maximum-impedance shots. Operators who try to bypass this limiter have destroyed the coil array, rendering the weapon inert. The black market offers bypass chips, but their reliability is disputed and their installation voids what little warranty the weapon carries.
specifications:
projectile: 3.2mm ferromagnetic tungsten dart
impedance stages: 12 selectable stages (subsonic to hypervelocity)
effective range: 40m (low impedance) / 600m (maximum impedance)
rate of fire: Semi-automatic
weight: 3.4 kg loaded
magazine capacity: 15 darts
thermal throttle: Forced 4-second cooling after 3 consecutive max-impedance shots
sound signature: Variable — near-silent at Stage 1, loud crack at Stage 12
power source: Integrated coil battery, 90 shots per charge at mixed impedance
tactical_use: Operators train with the VIR-9 across its full impedance range, developing the muscle memory to adjust the collar selector instinctively. Standard engagement doctrine opens at low impedance for target acquisition and confirmation, then adjusts upward based on the target's apparent armor profile. In urban environments, the ability to reduce sound signature dramatically without swapping weapons makes the VIR-9 extremely valuable for mobile operations. Military users value it for the flexibility it provides in asymmetric engagements where threat profiles change rapidly.
cultural_context: The VIR-9 is associated with serious professional operators who can afford expensive, complex equipment and have the training to use it effectively. It is not a weapon for the desperate or the untrained — the impedance selector is useless without proper calibration knowledge, and an operator who doesn't understand the thermal throttle will find themselves with a cooling rifle at exactly the wrong moment. Among Tessera Corponation's private security divisions, carrying a VIR-9 is a mark of senior field status. On the open market, its restricted classification means legitimate purchasers are vetted; black market copies often have degraded coil arrays from overuse.
story_hooks: A forensic investigator has recovered dart fragments from three separate crime scenes across different districts. The EM burn signature on each fragment indicates the same VIR-9 unit was used at each location — but the scenes span six weeks and the targets have no obvious connection. Someone is using a Switchback to work through a list, and no one knows whose list it is.

Tessera Corponation has quietly recalled a batch of VIR-9 units — serial numbers 9400 through 9650 — citing a 'coil calibration anomaly.' The recall notice went only to licensed retailers. The actual problem is that this batch was manufactured with a firmware error that causes the impedance selector to randomly spike to Stage 12 regardless of setting. Two operators have already been killed by the recoil. Tessera wants the units back before this becomes public.

A player acquires a VIR-9 and discovers its serial number has been filed down — but the coil battery's charge log still contains usage records from 47 previous engagements. Someone used this weapon extensively and then wanted it to disappear. The usage timestamps and impedance profiles tell a story if someone knows how to read them.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular linear accelerator rifle with a pronounced forward-swept profile. The barrel is notably thicker than conventional firearms, housing the magnetic coil array beneath a carbon-composite shroud. The overall impression is lean and purposeful—built for precision and adaptability rather than raw bulk. The trigger guard region features a distinctive rotating collar that breaks the rifle's otherwise streamlined silhouette.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 94 cm. Barrel length: 52 cm. Magazine well depth: 8 cm. Rotating impedance collar diameter: 4.2 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and manageable at 3.4 kg loaded—lighter than conventional rifle systems of comparable range, with weight distributed toward the receiver to reduce muzzle drift during impedance adjustments. Feels composed and stable in a two-handed grip despite the electromagnetic stress the system endures.
physical_description.primary_material: Carbon-composite barrel shroud over an aluminum alloy receiver frame. The coil array housing is reinforced steel with thermal management fins running along the upper surface. Ferromagnetic dart magazine is steel-bodied with transparent polymer witness window.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal gray with brushed aluminum accents on the receiver rails and charging handle. The barrel shroud has a subtly textured non-reflective coating. Heat dissipation fins along the top are burnished steel, showing early oxidation patterns from thermal cycling.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: gunmetal gray. Accents: brushed aluminum silver on controls and mounting points. Selector collar features anodized blue markings (stages 1-12) recessed into the rotating surface for tactile feedback.
physical_description.grip_texture: Wraparound ergonomic grip in high-traction rubberized polymer with subtle finger indexing. The charging handle is textured steel bar stock. The impedance selector collar has knurled edges for secure adjustment under stress.
distinctive_features: 12-stage rotatable impedance selector collar mounted coaxially around the trigger guard—operable without breaking firing grip
Thermal management fins running along the barrel shroud's upper surface, darkened from repeated heat cycling
Integrated ammo counter window on the magazine showing ferromagnetic dart stack
Subtle LED status indicator (green/amber/red) mounted on the left receiver rail, indicating thermal throttle state
Forward-swept barrel profile with slight downward rake, housing magnetic coil array
Recessed TESSERA CORPONATION logo stamped into the receiver just above the mag well
Modular rail system (MIL-standard equivalent) mounted above and below for sight and accessory attachment
Visible coil array housing seams running the length of the barrel shroud, suggesting internal complexity
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA CORPONATION stamped discreetly into the upper receiver. Model designation 'VIR-9' etched below the charging handle. Serial plate mounted on the left side of the receiver with alphanumeric identifier and manufacturing date code (GLMZ production line marked).
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but showing operational wear—minor scoring on the barrel shroud from field use, slight discoloration on thermal fins from heat stress cycling, and faint fingerprint patina on the rubberized grip from repeated use. Not battle-scarred, but clearly a working weapon rather than a showpiece.
